h1: East Hampton travel, stays & events guide
heroText: East Hampton, in the Hamptons, is the place for Main Beach, Georgica Beach, Guild Hall, the LongHouse Reserve and Mulford Farm. Its colonial history begins in 1639, when Lion Gardiner bought what became Gardiner's Island from the Montaukett people.

history.text: In 1639 Lion Gardiner purchased land, what became known as Gardiner's Island, from the Montaukett people.
During the War of 1812, the Gardiners used slaves to transport supplies back and forth to Gardiner's Island.
In 1831-1836, the Brothertown Indians migrated to Wisconsin, where they founded the settlement of Brothertown.
Pollock died in 1956 while driving with his mistress, Ruth Kligman, and a friend of hers, on Springs Fireplace Road, after picking them up at the Long Island Railroad station in East Hampton.

history.label: 1960s
history.text: The camp was designated as an Air Force Base supporting a 135-foot (41 m)-wide radar (AN/FPS-35) in the early 1960s to detect potential bombers headed for New York City.
The station was moved in 1966 to private property to save it from demolition by Joel Carmichael The Marine Museum itself was the former barracks for the Coast Guard.
In May 2007 the original Coast Guard station was moved to the property at the Town Marine Museum in Amagansett across the dunes from its original Atlantic Avenue beach location.

The Shinnecock Indian Nation, many of whom had continued to occupy a portion of land on the South Shore and claimed it as their reservation, received federal recognition in 2010 as a tribe and also have state recognition.
